---
title: "Compute cortisol response features"
output: html_document
---

Calculate response features from actual CARWatch collection times. Samples are
ordered by registered position, not by physical tube text.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(carwatch)

study_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "carwatch-gallery-cortisol-features")
generate_synthetic_study_data(
  study_dir,
  n_participants = 4,
  non_compliant_sample_ratio = 0,
  missing_awakening_time_ratio = 0,
  missing_sampling_time_ratio = 0,
  random_state = 42,
  create_cortisol_data = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

folders <- list.dirs(file.path(study_dir, "logs"), recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE)
participant_dirs <- stats::setNames(folders, basename(folders))
study_results <- convert_raw_logs(
  read_raw_logs_from_participant_dirs(participant_dirs),
  errors = "raise"
)
cortisol <- readr::read_csv(file.path(study_dir, "cortisol.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
merged_results <- merge_saliva(study_results, cortisol, match_on = "position")
```

```{r features}
features <- compute_features_from_carwatch(
  merged_results,
  saliva_type = "cortisol"
)

features
```

```{r inspect-times}
head(as_sample_events(merged_results)[, c(
  "participant", "day", "sample_position", "sampling_time", "time_min", "cortisol"
)])
```

AUC and slope values require complete, strictly increasing observed sampling
times within each participant-day curve.
